name: Persia: Empires of Fire and Poetry
description: From Cyrus and Persepolis to the Safavids and the modern republic: the long story of Iran's empires, its faith, and the poets who kept Persian alive.

checkpoints.name: Before the Persians
checkpoints.note: Elam was an old kingdom of the Iranian plateau, and Zoroastrianism, with its teaching about fire, truth and one wise god, took shape in these lands long before the great empire.

checkpoints.name: The first world empire
checkpoints.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire, and Darius the Great began Persepolis. Xerxes I fought the Greeks at Thermopylae and Salamis, and the empire fell to Alexander the Great after Gaugamela.

checkpoints.name: Parthians and Sasanians
checkpoints.note: The Parthian Empire held power between Rome and the east for centuries. The Sasanian Empire, which rivalled Rome and Byzantium, made Zoroastrianism its state faith and fell to Arab armies in the seventh century.

checkpoints.name: Poets and thinkers
checkpoints.note: After the Arab conquest Persian language and learning grew again. Avicenna wrote on medicine, Ferdowsi composed the Shahnameh, Omar Khayyam, Rumi and Hafez wrote poems still read across the world, and the Mongol Empire swept through the region in the thirteenth century.

checkpoints.name: The Safavid age
checkpoints.note: Safavid Iran made Shia Islam the faith of the state, and its rulers built a splendid capital. Later dynasties ruled a country pressed by neighbours and by European powers.

checkpoints.name: Monarchy and republic
checkpoints.note: The Pahlavi dynasty ruled from 1925 and modernised the state. The Iranian Revolution of 1978 and 1979 brought down the shah, and Ruhollah Khomeini became the leader of a new republic that went to war with Iraq from 1980 to 1988.
